history.titleZh: iPhone 18 Pro Max storage can drop lower than a hard drive at 1.1 MB/s during heavy writes — QLC NAND offers higher capacity but reportedly suffers 38% drop compared to TLC-based Pro
history.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware 报道，Apple 上周开售 iPhone 18 Pro 系列，其高容量存储版本采用基于 QLC 的 NAND 闪存，而非此前更常见的 TLC，这带来容量与性能之间的取舍。B站频道 Homolab 对 1TB iPhone 18 Pro Max 进行测试，并与 512GB TLC 版 iPhone 18 Pro 对比，发现 QLC 机型在持续重负载下存储性能会明显下降。

核心原理在于 NAND 每个存储单元保存的比特数不同：SLC 为 1 比特，TLC 为 3 比特，QLC 为 4 比特。QLC 每个单元有 16 种电平状态，而 TLC 为 8 种。因此 QLC 能在相同物理空间内提供更高容量，但写入时需要更精细的电压控制，速度更慢、出错率更高，通常也更依赖缓存和垃圾回收策略来掩盖短板。手机通常先用部分 NAND 模拟 SLC 缓存，获得极快写入；SLC 缓存耗尽后，再使用二级 TLC 缓冲；两级缓存都耗尽后，才直接写入 QLC NAND。存储占用越高，可用缓存越小，持续写入性能越差。

测试数据显示，在 4K 读取测试中，QLC 与 TLC 机型表现相近；但在低队列深度混合工作负载中，QLC 机型得分 8,168，TLC 机型得分 11,285，QLC 落后约 38%。在更重负载下，两者差距缩小，但 TLC 仍保持约 12% 优势。持续写入测试更能体现问题：1TB iPhone 18 Pro Max 的 SLC 缓存速度可达 3,000 MB/s；SLC 缓存耗尽后，二级 TLC 缓冲平均约 578 MB/s；当两级缓存都耗尽、必须直写 QLC NAND 时，持续写入速度可降至 79.4 MB/s，偶尔甚至低至 25.6 MB/s，已接近许多廉价 microSD 卡的水平，远慢于 microSD Express。存储开始填满后情况更糟：当容量用到 60%，可用 SLC 缓存从 250GB 骤降至 58GB，二级缓冲降至 396 MB/s，直写 QLC 平均仅 45 MB/s，偶尔低至 1.1 MB/s。

需要指出，这些是合成基准测试，代表较极端的最坏情况。日常网页浏览、消息、游戏、拍照等普通任务通常不会让用户感到明显问题。性能瓶颈更可能出现在 4K 或 ProRes 视频录制、大文件传输、数据备份恢复等存储密集型场景。总体来看，Apple 在高容量旗舰机型上采用 QLC，是以存储密度换取容量，适合更看重容量、写入负载不重的用户；但对经常处理大文件、高码率视频或频繁备份恢复的专业用户而言，高容量 QLC 机型可能在持续写入和缓存耗尽后明显不如 TLC 稳定。这也是 QLC 进入高端智能手机后需要面对的核心权衡。

history.title: From Enablement to Execution, Egypt’s AI Ecosystem Reaches Production Scale
history.description: Today, Egypt’s AI builders gathered in the Grand Egyptian Museum for a reception that highlighted the nation’s rapidly growing AI ecosystem — spanning AI natives, developers, researchers, startups and enterprises — building applications across industries. The event included a keynote from Paolo Guglielmini, vice president of EMEA at NVIDIA. Ahmed Mostafa, regional AI adoption lead […]
history.content: Today, Egypt’s AI builders gathered in the Grand Egyptian Museum for a reception that highlighted the nation’s rapidly growing AI ecosystem — spanning AI natives, developers, researchers, startups and enterprises — building applications across industries. The event included a keynote from Paolo Guglielmini, vice president of EMEA at NVIDIA. Ahmed Mostafa, regional AI adoption lead for the Middle East and Africa at NVIDIA, delivered a session on “Why Accelerating Every Layer Matters,” exploring NVIDIA’s full-stack approach to AI development and deployment. The event also featured a panel moderated by Basil Fateen, head of startups for the Middle East and Africa at NVIDIA, with participation from startups across smart spaces, healthcare, cybersecurity and robotics. In Egypt, the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute learner base grew more than tenfold in a single year. In June, the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority of Egypt licensed Hassan Allam Data Centers to build and operate data centers in the country. Under that license, Hassan Allam Utilities and investment firm A15 agreed to develop a new data center, an estimated $400 million investment. In addition, NVIDIA and A15 in July hosted an event connecting Egypt’s leading founders with NVIDIA’s global ecosystem. This has been complemented by recent startup and investor events in Egypt, including engagements with A15 and Plug and Play at the Creativa Innovation Hub at Sultan Hussein Kamel Palace, an affiliate of the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology. Spanning a range of industries, members of the NVIDIA Inception program in Egypt include: Aidera: A unified enterprise intelligence system that connects data, systems, workflows and operational touch points turning enterprise-wide signals into informed decisions, intelligent automation, coordinated execution and measurable impact. Intella: Developing Arabic speech intelligence for applications across financial services, telecommunications and more. Marses Robotics: Developing autonomous robotics and industrial automation technologies. Proteinea: Combining AI protein design with lab experiments to develop differentiated medicines. Stakpak: Developing an open source autonomous developer-operations AI agent. Paymob and Thndr: Building better financial services through technology and AI. The NVIDIA VC Alliance has also expanded its presence in Egypt, with A15 and M Empire joining the program, connecting more local investors with NVIDIA’s global startup ecosystem. This momentum has been complemented by startup and investor events, including collaborations with RiseUp and Plug and Play, as well as Flat6Labs, a regional entrepreneurship platform supporting startups and innovation across emerging markets, and Algebra Ventures, a Cairo-based venture capital firm backing technology startups. AI Growth Across Africa The Egypt ecosystem event showed just a piece of Africa’s larger, growing AI ecosystem. For most of the past decade, conversations about Africa’s AI ecosystem revolved around “potential.” They centered on what the technology might do for the continent, rather than what the continent could build with it. Africa is home to roughly 18% of the world’s population but less than 1% of the world’s data center capacity. This means African developers have often relied on cloud-based compute hosted outside the continent for large-scale AI training. This is rapidly changing. Within a year, four AI factories have been announced or brought online across Africa, with another 656 megawatts of new capacity in the pipeline. These AI factories will provide African developers and enterprises with the accelerated computing infrastructure needed to train, fine-tune and deploy AI models closer to where data is created. Cassava Technologies, Africa’s first NVIDIA Cloud Partner, is expanding access to NVIDIA accelerated computing through its AI factory in South Africa and planned deployments across Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria and Morocco — an investment that could reach $720 million. In Egypt, Cassava and Vodafone Egypt recently announced an AI factory initiative to provide businesses and government organizations with locally hosted AI infrastructure through GPU-as-a-service, supporting the development and deployment of AI applications while keeping data in-country. Building on Cassava’s first AI factory in South Africa, the rollout aims to expand access to local accelerated computing, helping developers, enterprises and researchers train, customize and deploy AI models closer to where their data is created. Similarly, Stratos Lab, a South African AI neocloud provider, is partnering with ECOBLOX and Digital Parks Africa to launch an AI cloud powered by more than 50 NVIDIA HGX B300 systems — delivering over 7 exaflops of performance. The deployment gives African enterprises and developers access to high-performance GPU compute locally, enabling model training, inference and agentic AI workloads with lower latency and at reduced costs. And at GITEX Africa in Marrakech in April, Nexus Core Systems announced a collaboration with Morocco’s Ministry of Digital Transition, its Ministry of Investment and the investment agency AMDIE to build the Nexus AI factory outside Casablanca: a $1.2 billion initial investment with 500 megawatts planned, NVIDIA Blackwell accelerated computing and renewable power from TAQA Morocco. The Demand Was Already There Infrastructure of this kind is not based on mere potential — it’s based on confidence that local developers and enterprises are ready to put the infrastructure to productive use. In 2024, NVIDIA set a target of training 100,000 developers across Africa through the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute within three years. To date, NVIDIA’s trained over 85,000 developers in Africa, and the continent is among NVIDIA’s fastest-growing developer regions — Nigeria is now the institute’s second-largest market globally. InstaDeep joined NVIDIA Inception in 2017 as a small team in Tunis using its first NVIDIA DGX system. Since then, it’s developed drug discovery, protein design and logistics optimization applications, and was acquired by BioNTech for about $680 million. Africa accounts for roughly a third of the world’s languages, often invisible to frontier models. To help advance African language models, language model lab Lelapa AI built InkubaLM and the Vulavula speech service for South African languages including isiZulu and Sesotho. MeetKai, for example, an NVIDIA Inception member, is expanding its work in Egypt with Smart Africa, building its AI stack on NVIDIA technology as part of its plans for the market. The company is among a growing group of AI innovators using NVIDIA technology to build and scale across Africa. And there’s still much room to grow. McKinsey puts African data center demand at roughly 0.4 gigawatts today, and estimates it will rise to between 1.5 and 2.2 gigawatts by 2030, which requires between $10 to $20 billion in construction. Learn more about the NVIDIA Developer Program, NVIDIA Inception and NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute.
history.author: Fatima Tambajang
history.titleZh: 从赋能到执行，埃及的人工智能生态系统达到生产规模
history.descriptionZh:
英伟达在埃及大埃及博物馆举办了一场接待活动，集中展示埃及快速成长的AI生态：参与者覆盖AI原生企业、开发者、研究者、初创公司与行业企业，应用横跨多个行业。英伟达EMEA副总裁Paolo Guglielmini发表主题演讲；英伟达中东和非洲区域AI采用负责人Ahmed Mostafa以“为什么加速每一层都很重要”为题，介绍英伟达面向AI开发与部署的全栈方法。活动还设有由英伟达中东和非洲初创业务负责人Basil Fateen主持的圆桌，参与初创企业来自智能空间、医疗健康、网络安全和机器人等领域。

在埃及，英伟达深度学习学院（DLI）的学习者规模一年内增长超过十倍。今年6月，埃及国家电信监管局向Hassan Allam Data Centers发放许可，允许其在埃及建设和运营数据中心。根据该许可，Hassan Allam Utilities与投资公司A15同意开发一座新数据中心，预计投资约4亿美元。7月，英伟达与A15还举办活动，将埃及领先创始人与英伟达全球生态连接起来。近期埃及还举行了多场初创与投资者活动，包括在通信与信息技术部下属的Sultan Hussein Kamel Palace的Creativa Innovation Hub与A15、Plug and Play的互动。

英伟达Inception计划在埃及的成员覆盖多个行业：Aidera提供统一企业智能系统，连接数据、系统、工作流和运营触点，将企业信号转化为决策、智能自动化、协同执行和可衡量影响；Intella开发面向金融服务、电信等场景的阿拉伯语语音智能；Marses Robotics研发自主机器人与工业自动化技术；Proteinea将AI蛋白质设计与实验室实验结合，开发差异化药物；Stakpak开发开源自主开发者运维AI代理；Paymob和Thndr则通过技术与AI改进金融服务。英伟达VC Alliance也在埃及扩展，A15和M Empire加入该计划，把更多本地投资者连接到英伟达全球初创生态。相关势头还得到RiseUp、Plug and Play、Flat6Labs以及开罗风投机构Algebra Ventures等活动的配合。

这场埃及生态活动只是非洲更大AI生态成长的一部分。过去十年，非洲AI讨论多围绕“潜力”，关注技术能为非洲做什么，而不是非洲能用技术构建什么。非洲拥有全球约18%的人口，却只占全球不到1%的数据中心容量，因此非洲开发者过去常依赖非洲以外的云端算力进行大规模AI训练。这一局面正在迅速改变：一年内，非洲已有四座AI工厂宣布或上线，另有656兆瓦新容量在管线中。这些AI工厂将为非洲开发者和企业提供加速计算基础设施，使其能在数据产生地附近训练、微调和部署AI模型。

非洲首家英伟达云合作伙伴Cassava Technologies正通过其南非AI工厂以及在埃及、肯尼亚、尼日利亚和摩洛哥的规划部署，扩大英伟达加速计算的可及性，投资规模可能达到7.2亿美元。在埃及，Cassava与Vodafone Egypt近期宣布AI工厂计划，通过GPU即服务为企业和政府机构提供本地托管的AI基础设施，支持AI应用开发与部署，同时将数据留在境内。南非AI新云提供商Stratos Lab则与ECOBLOX和Digital Parks Africa合作，推出由50多套英伟达HGX B300系统驱动的AI云，提供超过7 exaflops性能。该部署让非洲企业和开发者获得本地高性能GPU算力，以更低延迟和成本支持模型训练、推理和代理式AI工作负载。4月在马拉喀什GITEX Africa上，Nexus Core Systems宣布与摩洛哥数字转型部、投资部及投资机构AMDIE合作，在卡萨布兰卡郊外建设Nexus AI工厂：初期投资12亿美元，规划500兆瓦，采用英伟达Blackwell加速计算，并由TAQA Morocco提供可再生电力。

这类基础设施并非仅基于潜力，而是基于对本地开发者和企业已准备好有效使用算力的信心。2024年，英伟达设定目标：三年内通过DLI在非洲培训10万名开发者。截至目前，英伟达已在非洲培训超过8.5万名开发者，非洲是英伟达增长最快的开发者地区之一，尼日利亚已成为DLI全球第二大市场。InstaDeep于2017年以突尼斯小型团队身份加入英伟达Inception，使用其首套英伟达DGX系统，此后开发了药物发现、蛋白质设计和物流优化应用，并被BioNTech以约6.8亿美元收购。非洲拥有全球约三分之一语言，这些语言常在前沿模型中不可见。为推进非洲语言模型，语言模型实验室Lelapa AI构建了InkubaLM和Vulavula语音服务，覆盖isiZulu、Sesotho等南非语言。英伟达Inception成员MeetKai正与Smart Africa扩大在埃及的业务，基于英伟达技术构建AI栈，以推进其市场计划。越来越多AI创新者正使用英伟达技术在非洲构建和扩展业务。增长空间仍然很大：麦肯锡估计，非洲当前数据中心需求约0.4吉瓦，到2030年将升至1.5至2.2吉瓦，需要100亿至200亿美元建设投资。

从技术角度看，英伟达强调的“加速每一层”并非单点GPU优化，而是全栈加速：从底层加速计算平台、系统与网络，到CUDA-X库、AI框架和软件栈，再到上层模型、代理式AI与行业应用，各层都针对AI负载优化，以提升训练、微调、推理和部署效率。AI工厂则可理解为面向AI生产的专门化数据中心，通过本地化加速算力、GPU即服务和Blackwell/HGX等新一代系统，降低延迟与成本，并支持数据主权。其影响在于：埃及和非洲正从AI“消费者”转向AI“生产者”，在金融、医疗、语言、机器人、网络安全、药物研发和工业自动化等领域形成本地化应用，同时吸引投资、培育开发者并完善算力基础设施。

history.title: AMD Ryzen 5 5500F and 7500 show up at retail with pricing above MSRP — budget CPUs are $20 more expensive than list price, even from first-party sellers
history.description: Nearly two weeks after they were announced, AMD's Ryzen 5 5500F and 7500 (non-F) are available for sale, though prices are slightly above MSRP.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter AMD's new Ryzen 5 5500F and Ryzen 5 7500 are available for sale, though the prices are higher than AMD originally suggested. On Amazon, the Ryzen 5 5500F is available for $120, while the Ryzen 5 7500 is listed at $210, both $20 more expensive than AMD's suggested retail pricing. Both are sold directly by Amazon, suggesting we'll see slightly higher prices for these two chips than AMD originally suggested.Get the AMD Ryzen 5 5500F from AmazonGet the AMD Ryzen 5 7500 from AmazonAMD revealed the budget CPUs nearly two weeks ago, and despite launching on that date, the chips haven't been available for sale in the U.S. until now. The Ryzen 5 5500F is particularly interesting, as the $90 Ryzen 5 5500 has continually been among Amazon's best sellers in CPUs. Although the Ryzen 5 5500 and 5500F sound similar, there are actually quite a few differences between the two CPUs.Both are six-core, 12-thread chips using AMD's Zen 3 architecture, but the 5500 falls under the Cezanne family, while the 5500F falls under Vermeer. The 5500F comes with PCIe 4, compared to PCIe 3 on the 5500, as well as a higher 4.4 GHz boost clock — the base 5500 tops out at 4.2 GHz. These changes apparently allow the 5500F to achieve higher performance, somewhere in the range of 5% to 10%, in games. We'll be getting the CPU in the Tom's Hardware lab to test the performance ourselves.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Although Zen 3 is aging, it has become an ideal home for budget builders as the RAM pricing crisis continues to surge. In addition to the Ryzen 5 5500F, we saw AMD re-release the Ryzen 7 5800X3D earlier this year to combat rising DDR5 prices. Image 1 of 1 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 1 View Original We took the Ryzen 5 5500 (non-F) out for a spin earlier this year for a budget $100 CPU shootout. Generally, it underperforms the Intel competition at this price, but a 5% to 10% jump would close that gap. If performance holds up, the Ryzen 5 5500F may have a shot at our best CPUs for gaming list with its low price.The Ryzen 5 7500 is easier to parse. It's identical to the 7500F, just with integrated graphics. It comes with six Zen 4 cores for a total of 12 threads, and unlike the 5500, it exclusively supports DDR5 memory. The 7500 comes with a boost clock of 5 GHz and supports PCIe 5. Like the 5500F, it has a 65W TDP and comes bundled with AMD's Wraith Stealth cooler.AMD originally announced the Ryzen 5 5500F at $99 and the 7500 at $190, though the current Amazon listings are both $20 higher than that — $120 and $210, respectively. At the time of writing, the CPUs are only available at Amazon in the U.S.; Micro Center and Newegg don't have listings available. When other retailers pick up the chips, prices could come down.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThis isn't the first time we've seen oddly high prices on new AMD releases at Amazon. Earlier this year, the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 went up for sale on Amazon prior to release, selling for $1,000, $100 above MSRP. After the launch dust settled and listings went up at other retailers, the pricing dropped back down to $900. Hopefully, we'll see something similar happen here. history.author: Jake Roach
history.titleZh: AMD Ryzen 5 5500F and 7500 show up at retail with pricing above MSRP — budget CPUs are $20 more expensive than list price, even from first-party sellers
history.descriptionZh:
AMD新款入门级处理器Ryzen 5 5500F和Ryzen 5 7500已在美国亚马逊正式开售，但实际售价均高于AMD最初公布的建议零售价。其中Ryzen 5 5500F标价120美元，Ryzen 5 7500标价210美元，分别比官方建议价99美元和190美元高出20美元。两款产品目前均由亚马逊直接销售，且仅亚马逊有货，Micro Center和Newegg尚未上架。AMD大约两周前发布了这两款芯片，但直到现在才在美国市场铺货。当其他零售商开始销售后，价格有望回落。

Ryzen 5 5500F尤其值得关注，因为此前售价90美元的Ryzen 5 5500长期位居亚马逊CPU畅销榜。虽然名称相近，但5500F与5500存在显著差异。两者均为6核12线程、基于Zen 3架构，但5500属于Cezanne家族，而5500F属于Vermeer家族。5500F支持PCIe 4.0，而5500仅支持PCIe 3.0；5500F的加速频率提升至4.4 GHz，5500最高为4.2 GHz。这些改进使5500F在游戏中的性能提升约5%至10%。Tom's Hardware实验室将对其进行实测。在当前内存价格持续飙升的背景下，尽管Zen 3架构已显老旧，但它已成为预算装机者的理想选择。除5500F外，AMD今年早些时候还重新发布了Ryzen 7 5800X3D，以应对DDR5内存涨价。Tom's Hardware此前曾对Ryzen 5 5500进行过100美元级CPU对比测试，结果显示其性能通常不敌同价位英特尔竞品，但若5500F能实现5%至10%的提升，将有望缩小这一差距。如果性能表现稳定，凭借低廉价格，5500F有望跻身最佳游戏CPU榜单。

Ryzen 5 7500的定位则更为清晰。它本质上与7500F相同，只是增加了集成显卡。该芯片采用6个Zen 4核心，共12线程，仅支持DDR5内存，加速频率达5 GHz，并支持PCIe 5.0。与5500F一样，其TDP为65W，附赠AMD Wraith Stealth散热器。

价格方面，AMD最初宣布5500F为99美元、7500为190美元，但当前亚马逊售价均高出20美元。截至发稿，这两款CPU仅在美国亚马逊有售。这并非亚马逊首次出现AMD新品定价异常：今年早些时候，Ryzen 9 9950X3D2在正式发布前便以1000美元上架，比建议零售价高100美元，待其他零售商跟进后价格回落至900美元。此次情况或许类似。总体而言，5500F为仍在使用DDR4的预算玩家提供了更具性价比的升级选择，而7500则面向希望以较低成本进入DDR5/AM5平台的入门用户，两款产品在内存价格高企的当下各有明确的应用场景。

history.title: Huawei shelves global AI chip rollout as China's own demand outstrips supply — 15,488-chip Atlas clusters leverage optical networking to counter Nvidia, scales to 120 EFLOPS
history.description: Huawei says it will not offer its latest AI hardware outside of China citing lack of capacity to serve domestic demand.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Huawei's impressive next-generation Ascend 900-series AI accelerators will be offered only in China, not internationally, as the company struggles to meet domestic demand amid capacity constraints, the company announced this week. While the upcoming Ascend 960-series neural processing units (NPUs) could rival some of AMD's and Nvidia's existing AI GPUs, demand for these units outside of China was not guaranteed anyway.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI shortages (Image credit: Nvidia)AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supplyDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleChip scarcity assaults auto industry amid the worsening Nexperia and DRAM crisisThe custom AI ASIC state of play"Since we do not have enough capacity to even satisfy the ​demand in China, we do not have a plan to expand into the international market in a fully-fledged way," said Eric Xu, rotating chairman of Huawei, on the sidelines of the company's Huawei Connect conference, Reuters reports. He added that Huawei supplies limited volumes to 'some countries where demand is particularly strong,' though he did not elaborate.Huawei this week unveiled its latest AI accelerator roadmap, revealing major training and inference performance gains for its next-generation Ascend 960, 970, and 980 NPUs over the existing Ascend 910C and Ascend 950-series. The Ascend 960DT and 960PR are set to increase their FP8 training performance to 2 PFLOPS and their FP4 inference performance to 4 PFLOPS and 8 PFLOPS, respectively, in 2027. Meanwhile, their successors, Ascend 970 and Ascend 980, are projected to increase their FP4 performance to 14 PFLOPS and 28 PFLOPS, respectively, in the coming years.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Huawei Ascend vs Nvidia AI GPUs Swipe to scroll horizontally NPU FP8 Performance FP4 Perf Memory Memory Bandwidth Interconnect Bandwidth Targeted Release Nvidia H200 4 PFLOPS - 141 GB HBM3E 4.8 TB/s 900 GB/s 2023 Q4 Nvidia B300 10 PFLOPS 15/20 S/D PFLOPS 279 GB HBM3E 8 TB/s 1.8 TB/s 2025 Q4 Ascend 950PR 1 PFLOPS 2 PFLOPS 128 GB of HiBL 1.0 1.6 TB/s 2 TB/s 2026 Q1 Ascend 950DT 1 PFLOPS 2 PFLOPS 144 GB of HiZQ 2.0 4.0 TB/s 2 TB/s 2026 Q4 Nvidia R200 17.5 PFLOPS 35/50 T/I PFLOPS 288 GB HBM4 19.2 TB/s 3 TB/s 2026 Q4 Ascend 960DT 2 PFLOPS 4 PFLOPS 288 GB 9.6 TB/s 2.2 TB/s 2027 Q1 Ascend 960PR 2 PFLOPS 8 PFLOPS 192 GB 2.4 TB/s 2.2 TB/s 2027 Q3 Ascend 970 3.6 PFLOPS 14 PFLOPS 288 GB 14.4 TB/s 4.4 TB/s 2028 Ascend 980 7.2 PFLOPS* 28 PFLOPS* 384 GB 38.4 TB/s* 8 TB/s 2029 *Preliminary dataS/D - Sparse and DenseT/I - Training and InferenceBut while the upcoming Ascend NPUs will be considerably faster than their predecessors, particularly for inference, they will remain well behind Nvidia's previous- and current-generation accelerators, at least in raw compute performance. Huawei's 2027 Ascend 960DT is projected to deliver 2 FP8 TFLOPS for training, compared with Nvidia's 4 FP8 TFLOPS for the H200, released in 2023. The Ascend 960PR is expected to offer 8 FP4 PFLOPS for training, which is far behind Nvidia's B300, which delivers 15–20 NVFP4 PFLOPS. Even the Ascend 980, targeted for 2029, is projected to reach 7.2 FP8 PFLOPS and 28 FP4 PFLOPS, well below Nvidia's R200, which is on track to deliver 17.5 FP8 PFLOPS and 35/50 FP4 PFLOPS this year. You may like China’s Huawei to enter South Korean AI chip market with new Atlas SuperPods, clusters pack 8,192 Ascend 950 accelerators per deployment China's homegrown AI accelerators to supply 90% of the country's domestic market, analysts suggest Huawei details AI accelerator roadmap, pulls in next-generation Ascend NPUs by several quarters Such a massive performance difference with leading AI hardware will reinforce Huawei's reliance on massive system-level scaling rather than chip-for-chip performance to compete with Nvidia. But massive system-level scaling comes with massive power consumption, which will make Huawei's next-generation Atlas SuperPoDs and SuperClusters considerably less competitive in markets that can access hardware from AMD or Nvidia.Huawei is in an interesting paradoxical situation. On the one hand, its integration efforts like near-package optics (NPO) clearly free up capacity on 'older' nodes that can be used for other components of AI platforms. But on the other hand, SMIC's inability to ramp production on 7nm and 6nm-class nodes limits Huawei's ability to supply its AI hardware anyway, which is why it can barely meet demand.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThen again, while Huawei's Atlas SuperPoDs with up to 15,488 Ascend 960 NPUs can deliver up to 30 FP8 EFLOPS and 120 FP4 EFLOPS performance by far exceeding the capabilities of Nvidia's NVL72 clusters with a 72-GPU scale-up world size, their performance-per-watt is poised to be dramatically lower compared to Nvidia's architectures, which means that demand for such hardware outside of China will be limited at best. That said, a global AI hardware push doesn't make much sense for Huawei right now. What perhaps does make sense is offering cloud access to its hardware to various academic and research customers to popularize its CANN software stack.
