Then they will just use their iPhone because it has a big screen and potentially unfolds into an even bigger screen. So they’re kind of pointed at each other, each missing the thing the other one has. How do you think that gets resolved?Okay. I think Apple is terrified of whatever OpenAI is building, and we can talk about that. It’s a hockey puck-sized AI computer type of device that you talk to without a display or whatnot. I think Apple’s terrified. In fact, the latest development in their lawsuit is that Apple wants the court to show them and give them access to the upcoming device so they can analyze if it has any of their materials in it. So good luck to them on that one.At the same time, I do think Apple has the ability to fast-follow anything OpenAI does. If OpenAI puts out some remarkable product and it begins to hit steam, Apple’s just going to copy this thing and follow pretty fast. Unlike the smart glasses, where they’re coming five years, seven years after everyone else, I think if this donut or hockey puck thing is successful, Apple will follow them immediately.I think the models are getting commoditized to a point where they could fast-follow and have a very effective product. If Apple goes to Anthropic and says, “We want to copy this OpenAI device,” and obviously they’re not going to give us their secret sauce and models, “will you partner with us on this?” Yes. If they come to Google, “We need even better models. Could you partner on this?” Yes. Google has no legitimate hardware business that’s going to be destroyed over partnering with Apple on hardware. Anthropic has no hardware business. Apple can get this done.So yes, they’re afraid, on one hand. On the other hand, I really don’t think they need to be that worried because if it’s a success, they can just copy it, which is, I guess, what they’re accusing OpenAI of doing from the beginning anyway.In terms of the lawsuit, it is very clear that OpenAI employees have done some shady things. I’m surprised that the iPhone engineer, or former iPhone engineer, is at the center of the lawsuit; this is the one they’ve accused of taking material with him and sharing it with people and whatnot. I’m shocked that OpenAI has not cut bait on him and moved forward. I think their fear is that if they cut bait on this guy, employees are going to revolt.How could we trust working at a company like this if you are going to get sued by Apple, even a company that big, and you’re just going to cut bait on someone, right? So we’ll see what happens. We’ll see what happens. They’ve done shady things, but a lot of the stuff, as you said, is common business practice, stuff that Apple probably even does too.It’s very notable to me that none of the filings in the case so far have any mention of Jony Ive. Neither company wants to point out that Steve Jobs’ number two is at the center of all this because he’s leading the design of this product.I think it’s by design. I think it’s notable. And I even think the origin story of this lawsuit is Jony Ive himself. I think Apple’s point of view is that Jony Ive was on Apple’s payroll for half a decade or more after the Apple Watch. During that time, basically destroyed the Apple design team from within and took everyone with him to build a competitor to the products that he developed at Apple. That is Apple’s viewpoint.I think there’s a lot of anger towards Ive at the very center of this, particularly from Tim Cook and some of those other players there. I think Jony Ive’s perspective is that all the Apple products today are direct siblings of everything Jony Ive developed there. Even the iPhone Duo, you can see Jony Ive’s work in there. It’s all part and parcel with Jony Ive.I think that he believes that he created the product portfolio that’s the basis of this $3 to 4 trillion company. And he was tired after carrying that company post-Steve Jobs and very sad about Steve Jobs’ death, and wanted to move on. He and Tim Cook came to an agreement that he only needed to work at Apple for a few days a week. And so what? If he wants to eventually leave Apple and build something new and have people follow him, that’s up to them.So I think it’s two very different sides of the same story, and you can side with whoever you want to side with. But I think it’s really unfortunate that things did not work out for Apple and for Jony Ive together in this instance. I think he saw AI as the new core technology that he can develop something really cool around, just like the iPhone was developed around the cool technologies back then of the App Store, Multi-Touch, and what have you.What’s really interesting about that, and this is a whole different podcast, is that all of Ive’s best products are designed around limitations. The iMac was designed around the limitation of the CRT display. AI doesn’t have any limitations because it always just tells you it can do everything. I’m just dying to know what he identifies as the limitation that makes the magic of the next Ive product. As I said, that’s a whole different podcast, but it’s just on my mind as I think about what he might do to make this more than just a hockey puck that’s listening all the time.I’m psyched to play with it and to see it. And I think this screenless idea is both a blessing and a curse. I think that we’re going to really see how effective AI is when we’re using it without a screen and having it in the background.But at the same time, there are things about displays that are not replaceable with screenless devices. Gaming, massive market. Video conferencing, massive use case. Watching video, another massive market use case. I just don’t know how OpenAI takes over the world with a device that can’t video chat, can’t do gaming, and can’t do video. And we’ve seen historically that being an iPhone companion, that just doesn’t cut it.Actually, this brings me to you mentioning the AirPods with a camera. AirPods are a success because they have a huge attach rate to iPhones. People buy iPhones; they buy AirPods. People buy iPhones; they buy a set of AirPods. There you go. You got a huge business.And then you lose them every six months, or you break them, and you have to buy new ones. So it’s crazy.You mentioned that adding a camera to AirPods might turn them into a platform unto themselves. That would obviously compete with some of these screenless devices or these AI native devices. How would that work?Okay. These AirPods basically have the visual intelligence feature that you have on your iPhone. You could point at something. You can take action on it. You can get more information. It’s built into the AirPods. It’s no different. So one use case is that I’m on my computer, and I have my phone, and I want to add something to my calendar. I just point my iPhone camera at my email, and I say, “Add this to my calendar,” and it adds it to my calendar and parses all the links. The AirPods could do that for you now.You can tell your AirPods, “When I get to the pasta aisle at Whole Foods, stop me, ping me when you see the tomato sauce I’m looking for,” and it’ll do that. When you’re walking around a city, and you ask it to get directions to the nearest Walgreens, instead of telling you, “Turn right in 40 feet,” it’ll say, “Turn right by the black sedan parked at the corner.” So it uses visual information to provide you with context to help you throughout your day.It’s a game changer, I think, and I think it’s going to be a really sought-after product. And I think that the changes we saw with the AirPods 5 at this Apple event, where you’re now getting really solid ANC, even though it’s not inner ear, with some Pro features like the volume swipe at about 150 bucks, that’s a really good product at a really good price. I think that’s setting the stage for needing to make the AirPods Pro that much better. And that’s where the cameras come in as that core differentiator.This brings me to the last thing I want to talk to you about, which is Apple and privacy. The things you’re describing with AirPods are science fiction ideas that have been around forever. I tried Microsoft HoloLens 10 years ago, and they were doing augmented reality demos that are very much the things you’re describing. They had me change spark plugs in an ATV. I’ll never forget doing this with their big silly glasses on my face.The problem has been one: it’s very hard to shrink that technology and have the appropriate battery life. And then the other problem is, well, you’ve got a camera pointed at everything around you all the time, and people don’t like that.I’m always joking that I think the killer app for Meta’s glasses is facial recognition. If you just gave me a pair of glasses that would tell me everyone’s names and faces at events, I would be the single greatest politician in world history. The problem with that is that it requires a worldwide surveillance database of everyone taking each other’s pictures all day long. And that is probably not an appropriate trade-off for me to be the greatest politician in the world. But I’m just letting you know, I think that product would be cool for my personal benefit. The social cost would be too high.This is Apple’s brand — privacy — and they’re up against people calling the Meta glasses pervert glasses. They’re in a world where people hate Flock cameras and all the surveillance that’s happening online. They’re doing watchOS 27 with an always-on listening feature that just does transcripts. It doesn’t record or store any audio, but–Still a surveillance device. I’ll be honest with you. I can’t believe they did it.I can’t believe they did it.I can’t believe they did it.Right? It’s just listening, and you can double-click it, and it’ll show you a transcript of the last 15 seconds of what someone said to you without their permission.First of all, read the room.It doesn’t even light up.No, I know. No, that’s not true. It does light up. But read the room.I was told it doesn’t light up.Okay. First of all, we can get into this, but I was not at the Apple event for obvious reasons. I haven’t been at one since 2019.Well, you already know what’s going to happen.Well, I didn’t have the briefings.Yeah.But according to the literature on their website, when you’re doing that feature, it lights up with a microphone icon when you do the live rewind. Maybe it doesn’t light up for the Siri Recap — I don’t think it does for the all day listening — but the last 15 seconds things, it supposedly shows a microphone. But Nilay, is this podcast a video?Yeah.Okay. I’m wearing an Apple Watch. Can you see anything on my screen?Right, it’s crazy to me.So I can’t believe they did that because, really, you’re going to take a backlash like this and then do it again with a visual intelligence six, nine months from now?And then you’re going to do it with a pair of smart glasses, and you’re going to walk into all of the other things.Yeah.It feels like Apple knows that there’s a next generation of user interfaces coming that is AI-powered that requires an amount of ambient capture, whether that’s just listening so you can talk to it or whether it’s visual so you can see the world around you. And they haven’t solved the social privacy aspect.Nope.There are white papers about how Apple might have solved the technical database privacy aspect, right?Yep.They’ve got Private Cloud Compute, and they’re going to encrypt the data. They’re not going to store this and that. And I don’t think any of that’s going to overcome the social privacy aspect.They didn’t do a good job on articulating the social aspect of it at all. They could’ve shown more demos. They could’ve discussed it a bit deeper. I know they only have very limited time in the keynote, but I don’t think they spent enough time breaking things down here. I quite frankly think they did not do a good job rolling this feature out.I ask myself, would I be comfortable using this feature? Yeah. But then if I tell everyone around me in the last week, “Hey, I’ve been recording you the whole time,” they’re going to freak out, and they’re not going to trust Apple. So it’s a really interesting one. I’m pretty shocked they did it.What are the net new Apple Watch buyers because of this feature? What is the bigger challenge, doing this feature or not doing this feature? And I think that doing this feature is a bigger drawback than not doing the feature. Here, there is no cost of not doing something.Well, there is a cost if you think there’s about to be a wave of AI devices that are doing always-on transcripts and meeting recordings, and OpenAI is going to do something. I mean, we have seen a wave of startups that do this. But we’re not there yet, right?Right.This could’ve waited six months.So you can just foreclose it. This is like Microsoft stuff. You’re like, “Here’s a preview of a feature. Don’t even consider that stuff. Eventually this will get good,” and you’ve just foreclosed the competitor.Well, the other thing is they had nothing else for the watch, so they had to just do something, right? This is the weakest Apple Watch update we’ve seen in a long time, and they’re lost as to what to do next. Now they’re recalibrating it. They’re going to have a major watch revamp at the end of next year and so forth, but they have to do something.If it were me, I would have ripped off the bandaid at the same time with all the audio plus visual intelligence stuff next year. Do it all together and have a really coherent privacy story.But do you think that stuff is compatible with Apple’s reputation for privacy? This is the real question I’m getting at: they might not have told the right story about the Apple Watch. Apple is going to have to tell the right story about AirPods with cameras in them in a world where people are shooting spray foam at Flock cameras because they don’t want them in their communities. There’s a connection between these two ideas, and it doesn’t seem like Apple knows how to tell that story.Well, clearly not, because they haven’t done it. But here’s the story on the AirPods. They can’t record actual video. They can’t take actual pictures. They have an extremely low frame rate. I’m talking about a few frames per second.The actual data that gets input into them, it’s like… Have you ever used a Roomba, and when you look at the app, what does the Roomba see? It’s like wireframes of the environment. It would not be able to tell you and me apart. It’s just seeing two people.Then how can it do the brands of tomato sauce in the aisle?Well, in terms of non-people, it’d be able to do that, and it could read text. So it’d be pretty heavily reliant on reading text and seeing color and whatnot. But being able to differentiate between two people would be very difficult. It’s almost like a fake reproduction of what’s around you. I don’t have a good explanation for it, but I’m sure if they wanted to, they’ll give a good one.I’m not sure they’re going to break it down. They might just say, “Just trust us. We’re Apple. It’s not taking pictures. It’s not taking video. It doesn’t know what it’s seeing to some extent.” So we’ll see how they play it. But I would’ve done all this stuff together, ripped off the bandaid and spent a lot of time focused on it. There was no need to do this audio intelligence feature at the end of ‘26 when you could have done it at the end of ‘27.Unless you’re trying to slowly boil the frog, right? You’re going to get people mad about this, and then you’re going to do the next one the next time. Right.It just seems like this next generation of devices involves some kind of ambient listening that we are not ready for as a society. People are really mad about Meta glasses. What are you going to do about it?They soiled the water for Apple and a lot of other companies. Meta being the first mover on this created an industry-wide problem. And I think even though Apple has such a strong privacy stance, there are people who don’t believe them. There are people who don’t care what they have to say. There are people who are going to be angry about the Apple glasses and whatnot.I think Apple, to some extent, is on such a high horse with its privacy message that it came away surprised that there would be some backlash to Apple doing this. They think, I believe, that people are overblowing it when it comes to Apple and everyone should just be focused on Meta. And just because Meta has done a poor job protecting people’s privacy doesn’t mean we’re going to. So we’ll see what happens.One thing: when I talk to the folks there, they never make the connection between Apple and Meta in the sense that Meta’s apps run on Apple’s phones. People are mad about Meta, and they still think the phones, Apple’s phones, are listening to them, and they can’t quite make that connection because it undoes a lot of their own messaging. If you believe your iPhone is listening to you, that’s not just Meta’s problem. It is also Apple’s problem.They kind of have to actively ignore that relationship because otherwise everything else falls apart. And I think that’s why there’s this blind spot. If people’s watches start generating transcripts, it’s exactly the same relationship as “my iPhone is listening to me, and that’s why I saw an ad for a vacation that I only talked to my friend about.”I’m curious what they’re going to do. I have a feeling they’re just going to bulldoze their way through it. They’re going to just try to tell a good story. They’re going to do a ton of PR briefings about it. They’re going to do a ton of white papers about it, and get as nerdy and in-depth as they can on this stuff.You know what they’re going to do? They’re going to throw out a lot of comparisons. I even heard Ternus do this in one of the interviews, in Apple’s statement on some of these features. I could totally imagine them saying, “Why is it any different recording from smart glasses if you could just hold your phone up and record people?” With the audio intelligence feature, one thing I didn’t even think of is the Apple Watch-It’s very funny you just mentioned that because that is exactly what Mark Zuckerberg just said to our friend Alex Heath.Oh, that’s funny.“How is it different from a phone?” This is the industry’s approach. I think the answer is that people are like, “Yeah, I can see you doing that, and I feel very comfortable telling you to stop.” There’s something different about that.I didn’t even realize this. Someone pointed this out to me the other day. It’s like your Apple Watch has had the Voice Memos app for, I don’t know, eight years at this point. Who stopped anyone from recording their whole day with the Voice Memos app on the Apple Watch anyway? This is just a more privacy-centric version of that. So Apple’s solving a problem here. They’re not creating one. So it just depends on how you look at these things. I think they’ll bulldoze their way through it. It’s going to be a problem, but I think they’ll be fine.All right. Last two before I let you get out of here. We’ve talked around the iPhone Duo a lot. We’ve mentioned it a lot. It’s the thing that just came out. We haven’t talked about it. What do you think of it?I think it’s incredible. I think, and this is a bold take, that foldables will become the new normal within a decade. If you look at the market share of smartphones at the end of 2006, smartphones had like 6 percent of the market. Now they have 85 percent of the market. It went over 50 percent of the market after five to six years.The iPhone itself was not the source of that, but the iPhone got everyone into the smartphone game. I think the iPhone Duo is going to do the same for the phone market. I think it’s going to become the new normal.Even though Apple is a late mover to foldables?Yeah. I think the Apple brand is that strong, really. I really do. I think the fit and finish, the software integration, is going to get people really excited about this category. I think that the Apple Upgrade program, the leasing program, will eventually expand internationally. I think that’s going to get people in it.I think that at some point they’re going to stop advertising sticker prices and focus on the monthly prices, and they’re going to get people locked into this thing. They’re going to have a family of iPhone Duos over time. You’ll see every phone maker just transitioning, transitioning to foldables. Samsung: half the line is already foldables. Very soon the candy bar style is going to become legacy.That’s a big prediction. Although I will say their iPhone handoff feature, where you can move a number between phones, seems to point to a future where I, for example, have the folding phone for work and then a much smaller, lighter phone for the weekends with the family. You can see that vision taking shape only because it’s now easy to port a number between devices, just whenever you want, which I think is incredible. Last question. We’ve talked a lot about Apple, its culture, and its set of products. What do you think its biggest challenges are in the new era under John Ternus, and what do you think its biggest opportunities are?I would say that I think the biggest challenge and the biggest opportunity are the same thing. Ternus’ Apple for the next three to five years is still Tim Cook’s Apple, right? That’s just the reality. He’s still going to be there in the background. He’s still going to loom large, and the product pipeline is still going to be coming out of an era that started under Tim Cook.But in five years from now, they are going to need to start thinking of what actually replaces the iPhone as the next thing. We went from the Mac to iCloud to AI as the center. What is Apple’s new thing after the phone? What is Apple’s new thing after the current generation of AI? And Ternus’ tenure as CEO, I think, will go down as a success if he’s able to find that next new centerpiece. He’s got a few years before he needs to start cooking on that, but I’m talking about something that can be in development for 5 to 10 years.Tim Cook never had the opportunity to have his new centerpiece of the company. He never had the opportunity to put his stamp on products at the company for two reasons. Both things that he tried to do as his centerpiece failed spectacularly. Obviously the Vision Pro, but the car — the car, that was Apple’s multi-trillion-dollar market cap opportunity, and they just blew it. Ternus will need to successfully hit that.I’d actually put a third thing on that list. It was the very beginning of the Cook era, with Jobs literally on his deathbed, and he said he’d figured out TV. Oh, yes.He had to spend however long pretending he knew what that meant because I don’t think it had been solved. And so there was this first wave of “Apple’s going to redefine TV” because the last page of the Isaacson biography had a Jobs quote on it.They haven’t even done a new Apple TV box in four years.That’s a long time. It’s funny because you don’t need one. It never occurs to me that I need to upgrade this thing, but maybe there’s going to be some AI feature.Well, Siri AI. They’ve been waiting for the Siri AI update. This could be a whole other podcast, but Siri AI has been the gate to all of these new product categories. The AirPods were supposed to be out already, the Apple TV, the HomePod, the smart home hub… all these devices were supposed to come out. Apple couldn’t do any of them until Siri AI. Now Siri AI is here, so the floodgates are open.All right. Well, Mark, we’re going to have to have you back on the show to talk about those floodgates and all these new products very soon. I can’t believe you haven’t been on until now. Thank you so much for being on Decoder.Yeah. And obviously I’d love to have you on my new podcast, Power On Podcast, launching very shortly. So thanks in advance.Questions or comments? Hit us up at decoder@theverge.com. We really do read every email!Decoder with Nilay PatelA podcast from The Verge about big ideas and other problems.SUBSCRIBE NOW!
history.author: Nilay Patel
history.titleZh: 约翰·特努斯能否为苹果找到下一个大事件？
history.descriptionZh:
这篇 Decoder 访谈围绕苹果在 John Ternus 接任 CEO 后的首场 iPhone 发布会、首款折叠机 iPhone Duo、AI 战略、领导层大换血、隐私争议以及与 OpenAI/Jony Ive 的竞争诉讼展开。彭博社首席苹果记者 Mark Gurman 与主持人 Nilay Patel 对谈，核心判断是：苹果正在从 Tim Cook 时代过渡到 Ternus 时代，但未来三到五年仍会带有强烈的 Cook 烙印；真正决定 Ternus 成败的，是他能否为苹果找到 iPhone 之后的下一个核心平台。

**一、Ternus 首秀与 iPhone Duo：苹果刻意安排的“新时代”**
苹果此次发布会是 John Ternus 接替 Tim Cook 后不到两周内的首次重大产品发布，也是苹果首款折叠手机 iPhone Duo 的亮相。Gurman 认为，这两件事同时发生并非巧合。苹果有意让 Ternus 成为新产品时代的门面，而不是让 Cook 在任内最后阶段拿走折叠机、AI 原生设备等产品的功劳。发布会本身与 Cook 时代风格接近，甚至“可以互换”，但 Ternus 开场就谈 AI 和“智能个人中心”，显露出与 Cook 不同的管理风格：Cook 更倾向协商式、集体决策，会不断追问；Ternus 则更愿意直接做决定、表达观点，哪怕别人不同意。

Nilay 指出，“智能个人中心”很像当年 Steve Jobs 把 iMac 称为数字中枢的翻版，而 iPhone Duo 以“One more thing”收尾，整体像是在让新 CEO 穿上旧 CEO 的衣服、唱苹果的“金曲”。Gurman 同意苹果在讲故事时非常保守，但也认为苹果是在用手里的牌讲最好的故事。关键问题是：苹果在 2026 年 9 月办了一场重大发布会，却没有推出真正引人注目的新 AI 功能，前 15 分钟基本是在重新叙述过去两年的 Apple Intelligence。苹果没有 AI 原生核心设备，只能继续把 iPhone 包装成 AI 设备，直到有新的杀手级硬件出现。

**二、AI 路线图：六款 AI 原生设备与“Google 过渡方案”**
Gurman 透露，未来一年半左右约有六款 AI 原生设备将出现。第一款是智能家居中枢，形态类似 Amazon Echo Show，但采用苹果风格：方形屏幕、全新操作系统，本质是“Siri AI 操作系统”，支持对讲、视频会议、主动智能，并可通过 AI 版 Face ID 识别用户、显示个性化内容。苹果还在做家庭安防系统，以及带机械臂的智能家居中枢版本——放在桌上可移动，这类产品在亚洲和中国市场正热。之后是智能眼镜，Gurman 仍认为会在 2027 年推出并上市；还有带摄像头的 AirPods，以及其他可穿戴设备。

但苹果的 AI 底层能力是短板。Gurman 批评苹果长期奉行“Cook 信条”：要拥有和控制所有基础技术，甚至为了蜂窝调制解调器收购并修复 Intel 基带业务，却没能拥有前沿 AI 模型。苹果高管曾说“我们从未拥有搜索，也不需要拥有 AI”，Gurman 认为这很荒谬。苹果内部原计划把 Google 模型作为过渡，直到自研模型成熟，但 Gurman 看到很少证据表明苹果正在重新全力自研、进行大型 AI 收购或高薪挖 AI 研究员。苹果可能在观望 Google 合作效果、Anthropic/OpenAI IPO 以及 AI 安全监管，再决定下一步。Siri 能力不足反而被调侃为“至少不会杀死全人类”。

对比来看，Nilay 提到 Meta 同周推出 Muse，扎克伯格给用户 8GB 云端存储和 8GB 云端 RAM，能做很多 iPhone 端 AI 做不到的事。这凸显苹果在端侧 AI 和云侧 AI 上的压力。

**三、领导层大换血：Cook 时代的“Hotel California”与 Ternus 的新班底**
Gurman 详细梳理了苹果领导层更替：2023 年起 Cook 开始认真推动继任计划。CFO Luca Maestri 于 2024 年底退休，由 Kevan Parekh 接任；COO Jeff Williams 于 2025 年退休，由 Sabih Khan 接任；总法律顾问 Kate Adams 在 2026 年过渡，由来自 Meta 的 Jennifer Newstead 接替；2026 年底，Cook 交棒给 Ternus。Cook 转任执行主席，仍会发挥巨大影响。

Gurman 称苹果采用“Hotel California”策略：高管退休后仍以半退休、顾问、特殊项目等方式留在公司。Phil Schiller 离开 App Store 和 Apple Events 职责，转做特殊项目并直接向 Ternus 汇报，但仍留在苹果领导层页面。部分原因是 Ternus 和 Eddy Cue 希望进一步挖掘 App Store 变现，而 Schiller 认为监管机构和开发者仍对苹果不满，想保持距离。美国司法部针对 App Store、CarPlay 等的反垄断案仍在继续。

硬件负责人 Johny Srouji 被任命为“首席硬件官”，这是苹果新设头衔，也使他成为 Ternus 之下第二重要的人物。Srouji 打造了 Apple Silicon，并主导了苹果自研调制解调器——苹果收购 Intel 基带业务后将其修复，新手机已采用，甚至为让自研基带显得有竞争力而放缓高通基带。但 Gurman 认为 Srouji 不会长期留任，可能一两年内再次考虑离开，而苹果没有具备同等行业威望的继任者，未来可能不得不拆分硬件工程团队。

设计方面，Jony Ive 离开后，苹果不再有传奇级别的首席设计官；Alan Dye 去了 Meta，设计负责人降为 VP 并向 Ternus 汇报。苹果可能重新走向职能型结构，但也面临 VP 层人才流失：Eddy Cue 等资深 SVP 长期不走，下面的人晋升无望。Gurman 认为苹果可能增设层级，例如让 Craig Federighi 出任首席软件和 AI 官，以留住人才。他判断，除了 AI，苹果最大的问题之一就是关键人才保留；而缺乏年轻、有颠覆性想法的高管梯队，也影响了苹果对 AI 的早期判断。

**四、隐私、Apple Watch 与带摄像头 AirPods**
苹果在 watchOS 27 中推出全天候监听转写功能，可显示最近 15 秒对话的转录，但不录制或存储音频。Gurman 和 Nilay 都对此感到震惊，认为这在社交隐私上非常敏感。苹果知道下一代 AI 用户界面需要环境感知——要么持续聆听，要么视觉捕捉世界——但尚未解决社会接受问题。苹果有 Private Cloud Compute 等技术隐私方案，却没有把社会隐私故事讲清楚。

带摄像头的 AirPods 被 Gurman 视为下一个平台级产品。它不能拍视频或照片，帧率极低，只有每秒几帧，输入数据类似 Roomba 的线框环境图，难以区分具体的人，但能读文字、识别颜色和物体。应用场景包括：指向某物获取信息并操作；把邮件内容加入日历；在超市走到番茄酱货架时提醒；在城市导航中说“在街角黑色轿车旁右转”，而不是“40 英尺后右转”。AirPods 5 以约 150 美元提供不错的 ANC 和音量滑动等 Pro 功能，为未来 AirPods Pro 用摄像头做差异化铺路。

但 Nilay 指出，Meta 眼镜已让公众对可穿戴摄像头高度警惕，Flock 摄像头也引发社区反感。苹果即使强调隐私，也可能遭遇强烈反弹。Gurman 认为苹果可能会通过大量 PR、白皮书和“这和手机拍摄有何不同”的类比强行推进，但社会隐私问题不会因此消失。

**五、OpenAI/Jony Ive 诉讼与竞争**
Jony Ive 与 Sam Altman 合作，许多苹果设计师加入 OpenAI。苹果起诉 OpenAI 窃取内部信息和产品计划，OpenAI 称只是正常招聘和商业行为。苹果甚至要求法院允许其检查 OpenAI 即将推出的设备，以判断是否包含苹果材料。Gurman 认为苹果非常害怕 OpenAI 的硬件——一个冰球大小、无屏幕、以语音交互为主的 AI 计算机。但他也认为，如果该产品成功，苹果可以快速跟进，因为模型正在商品化，苹果可以找 Google 或 Anthropic 合作。诉讼中，一名前 iPhone 工程师被指向 OpenAI 带走材料；OpenAI 未与他切割，可能担心员工反弹。双方文件都未提 Jony Ive，但 Gurman 认为苹果愤怒的核心正是 Ive：苹果认为他在 Apple Watch 之后仍领取苹果薪水多年，却从内部瓦解设计团队并带走人才，去打造竞争对手。Ive 则可能认为今天苹果产品组合都源自他的设计遗产，他因 Jobs 去世疲惫而选择离开。Ive 把 AI 视为新的核心技术，但 Nilay 提出一个有趣问题：Ive 最擅长的产品都围绕限制设计，而 AI 看似没有限制，他如何围绕 AI 的限制做出下一个革命性产品，仍待观察。

**六、iPhone Duo 与折叠屏前景**
Gurman 对 iPhone Duo 评价极高，甚至给出大胆预测：折叠屏将在十年内成为新常态。2006 年底智能手机仅约 6% 市场份额，如今约 85%，并在五六年内超过 50%。iPhone 当年推动了智能手机普及，iPhone Duo 可能同样推动折叠机普及。苹果虽是折叠机晚到者，但品牌、做工、软件整合、Apple Upgrade 租赁计划、月付定价和家庭化产品线会吸引用户。三星已有一半产品线是折叠机，糖果 bar 形态将逐渐变成 legacy。苹果的 iPhone 号码转移功能也预示未来：工作用折叠机，周末用更小更轻的手机。

**七、Ternus 时代的最大挑战与机会**
Gurman 认为，Ternus 未来三到五年的苹果仍是“Cook 的苹果”：Cook 作为执行主席仍在背后，产品管线也来自 Cook 时代。五年后，苹果必须找到取代 iPhone 的下一个中心。Cook 从未真正留下自己的新核心产品：Vision Pro 和造车项目都失败，电视也未真正解决，Apple TV 盒子已四年未更新。Siri AI 曾是 AirPods、Apple TV、HomePod、智能家居中枢等新品类共同的闸门；现在 Siri AI 到来，闸门打开，苹果将迎来一波新产品。Ternus 的成败，将取决于他能否在这波产品中为苹果找到下一个“新中心”。

history.title: New RTX 5070 Autumn Limited Edition gaming GPU doubles as an air freshener with built-in 'e-sports aromatherapy' — AX Gaming's white and purple card also features an anime character and floral graphics
history.description: AX Gaming has revealed its latest seasonal anime-themed limited edition graphics card which, this time, is designed to please your nose as much as your eyes.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter AX Gaming has revealed its latest seasonal anime-themed limited-edition graphics card, which, this time, is designed to please your nose as much as your eyes. The Inno3D subsidiary has released similarly styled GPUs before, but new for Autumn / Fall is the “innovative e-sports aromatherapy” component in its GeForce RTX 5070 12G Autumn Limited Edition (machine translation).Smellivision is included as part of this limited edition. The graphics card maker says this product delivers a form of aromatherapy. You will be able to smell the “autumn-like” aroma even from a cold start, it says. There is no information about aroma oil refills. It would be good to see the fragrance module to see how this subsystem works. Screenshot + Google Translate (Image credit: AX Gaming )The anime character you see in the main picture, and who stars on the metal backplate, is called ‘Snow Li.’ She sits with the GeForce RTX logo to one side, with an Autumn / Starry Moon motif beneath it. To the right is an ornate venting pattern for the third fan to push air through the cooling fins.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: AX Gaming’s substantial triple-fan card features a white-purple gradient wrapping around. “The fan blades are printed with exclusive logos such as Osmanthus, AX, and Star and Moon, making it lively and exquisite,” the maker romanticizes. “The edges of the chassis are decorated with colorful maple leaves and tiny star patterns, like starlight falling on a maple forest on an autumn night.” We also note this isn’t just a vinyl wrap. AX Gaming highlights that the design mixes “UV printing and multi-surface engraving techniques.” Even the fan blades have some logos.This seasonal graphics card release has ARGB maple leaf lighting, and its “flower-shaped ventilation holes are inlaid with LEDs and support synchronized lighting effects.” Also, perhaps difficult to believe, AX Gaming says that the light and shadows thrown by the powered-up graphics card “creating a full-on autumn night starry night atmosphere.” You may like Nvidia created a set of trading cards featuring iconic moments from the company's history The only current-generation graphics card on sale below MSRP AMD RX 9070 GRE collapses to $499 to save 1440p gaming (Image credit: AX Gaming )Beyond the visuals and fragrance, this is an ordinary but decent-sounding RTX 5070. You’ll still get your 6,144 CUDA cores, 12GB of GDDR7, and agreeable AAA gaming performance with access to GeForce features. Some non-cosmetic design choices that are welcome include the dual-layer metal magnetic backplate, five 8mm ultra-thick composite heat pipes, and the hidden power cabling.In its press release, AX Gaming says the "Autumn Stars and Moon, Maple Leaves in Full Bloom" themed card is a strictly limited (quantity/time) release. That’s bound to make it even more expensive than a regular RTX 5070, if you can order/reserve one.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
history.author: Mark Tyson
history.titleZh: 新款RTX 5070秋季限定版游戏GPU兼具空气清新功能，内置“电竞香薰”——AX Gaming的白色与紫色显卡还配有动漫角色和花卉图案
history.descriptionZh:
知名显卡品牌AX Gaming（映众Inno3D旗下子品牌）日前发布了其最新一季的动漫主题限量版显卡——GeForce RTX 5070 12G Autumn Limited Edition（秋季限量版）。与此前推出的同类风格产品一样，这款新卡延续了季节限定的路线，但最大的不同在于它主打一项颇具话题性的新卖点：内置"电竞香薰"（e-sports aromatherapy）组件，官方宣称即使是从冷启动状态，用户也能闻到带有"秋日气息"的香气。也就是说，这张显卡不仅要取悦眼睛，还想"照顾"你的鼻子，外媒Tom's Hardware形象地将其称为"气味视觉"（Smellivision）。

不过，目前官方并未透露香薰精油如何补充或更换，也没有展示香薰模块的具体结构，因此这一子系统的实际工作原理仍有待观察。

在外观设计上，这款显卡采用了三风扇散热结构，整体为白紫渐变配色。显卡金属背板上印有一位名为"Snow Li"的动漫角色，其身旁是GeForce RTX标识，下方点缀"秋月/星月"图案；背板右侧则是为第三颗风扇设计的华丽开孔通风纹样，用于将气流吹向散热鳍片。官方描述称，风扇叶片上印有桂花、AX、星月等专属标识图案，机身边缘装饰有彩色枫叶和细小星点，营造出"秋夜星光辉映枫林"的观感。值得注意的是，这并非简单的贴膜工艺，AX Gaming强调其采用了"UV打印与多表面雕刻"相结合的混合工艺，连风扇叶片上都带有标识。

灯光方面，这款季节限定卡配备ARGB枫叶灯效，其"花形通风孔内嵌LED灯珠，并支持灯效同步"。AX Gaming甚至表示，显卡点亮后投射出的光影能营造出"完整的秋夜星夜氛围"。

抛开视觉与气味这些"非功能性"卖点，这本质上仍是一张规格标准的RTX 5070。核心规格包括6144个CUDA核心和12GB GDDR7显存，可提供令人满意的大型3A游戏性能，并完整支持GeForce系列的各项功能特性。一些颇具诚意的非外观设计包括：双层金属磁吸背板、5根8mm超厚复合热管，以及隐藏式供电走线设计。

AX Gaming在新闻稿中表示，这款以"秋月星辉，枫叶正盛"为主题的显卡为严格限量发售（限数量、限时间）。这也意味着，即便能够预订或购买到，其价格几乎必然高于普通版RTX 5070。

history.title: Snag the least expensive 32GB DDR5-6000 memory kit available for only $429 — $40 off promo code for V-Color Manta XSky yields the least expensive DDR5-6000 CL30 kit available right now
history.description: Buy 32GB of V-Color Manta XSky RAM for only $429. This capable, white DDR5-6000 CL30 kit is one of the best deals out for the speed and timings
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter RAM prices have been out of this world for nearly a year, with some 32GB kits frequently breaking $500. The only real relief we had came from RAM combo deals, where you get a motherboard, processor, and RAM at a discount. While that well has seemingly run dry, at least for the moment, we did find a solid deal for the times on a 32GB V-Color Manta XSky DDR5-6000 kit for $429 when using promo code TEF366 at Newegg, making it the least expensive DDR5-6000 CL30 kit around (by ~$70) at Newegg. Check out this deal at Newegg Deals like this, and the combos when active, are by far the best way to buy new RAM in the ongoing RAMpocalypse. Gone are the days when you can get 64GB of DDR5-6400 RAM for $225 (what I paid for a G.Skill Trident Z Royale kit in April 2025), and you’re left with what we have now…the best prices in an extremely difficult market.As for this specific kit, it’s a great option for any build, performance-wise. The DDR5-6000 speed isn’t the fastest kit out there, but it does sit squarely in AMD’s sweet spot for price-to-performance and is much faster than older DDR4 modules. Sadly, we didn’t review this specific kit, but below are performance numbers from a similar DDR5-6000 CL30 kit from Team Group that show how well that speed and timings perform in our CPU test suite.Save $50V-Color Manta XSky 32GB DDR5-6000 CL30 (White): was $479.99 now $429.99 at AmazonUpgrade to DDR5 with the least expensive DDR5-6000 CL30 kit we can find in the V-Color Manta XSky (white) RAM kit. Use promo code TEF366 to take $40 off the listed $469.99 price.View Deal (Image credit: Future)The Manta XSky kit includes two white DDR5-6000 modules with CL30-38-38-96 timings at 1.35V. These speeds and timings work well for any use case, from gaming to workstation productivity, and you’ll get the most out of your system at these speeds, especially on the AM5 platform. If you were considering this kit for an Intel system, it will also work well. A frosted RGB light bar across the top of the sticks adds some bling to your chassis. If you need a black kit, V-Color has their Manta XFinity DDR5-6000 CL30 kit for only $439 using promo code TEF364.While $429 with promo code TEF366 for a 32GB set of RAM makes me want to cry (considering I bought 64GB for about half of this price in early 2025), it’s one of the best deals available. As a matter of fact, it is the least expensive DDR5-6000 CL30 available at Newegg or Amazon, and it doesn’t force you to choose between reasonable timings/speeds and price/performance. If you’re in the market to start a DDR5-based build or upgrade what you have, I wouldn’t pass this Newegg deal up.
history.author: Joe Shields
history.titleZh: Snag the least expensive 32GB DDR5-6000 memory kit available for only $429 — $40 off promo code for V-Color Manta XSky yields the least expensive DDR5-6000 CL30 kit available right now
history.descriptionZh:
近一年来，内存价格持续处于异常高位，32GB 套件经常突破500美元。此前唯一明显缓解来自内存组合优惠，即主板、处理器和内存打包折扣，但目前这类优惠似乎也暂时枯竭。在此背景下，Newegg 出现一个相对划算的促销：V-Color Manta XSky 32GB DDR5-6000 CL30 白色内存套件，使用优惠码 TEF366 后约429美元（列表价469.99美元减40美元；亚马逊同款也标称从479.99美元降至429.99美元）。它成为 Newegg 上能找到的最便宜 DDR5-6000 CL30 套件，比同类产品低约70美元。作为对比，2025年4月还能以225美元买到64GB DDR5-6400 G.Skill Trident Z Royal 套件，如今市场已大不相同。

规格方面，该套件为两条白色 DDR5-6000 模块，总容量32GB（2×16GB），时序 CL30-38-38-96，电压1.35V，顶部带磨砂 RGB 灯条。DDR5 相比 DDR4 采用更高频率和带宽、双32位子通道、片上 ECC 和板载电源管理等设计，能在更低电压下提升能效与数据吞吐。6000 MT/s 虽非最快，但正好落在 AMD AM5 平台性价比甜点，也明显快于老 DDR4；对 Intel 平台同样兼容。若需要黑色版本，V-Color Manta XFinity DDR5-6000 CL30 使用优惠码 TEF364 为439美元。

性能上，该具体套件未经过评测，但类似 Team Group DDR5-6000 CL30 套件在 CPU 测试中表现良好，说明该频率和时序适合游戏、工作站生产力等场景。技术影响与购买建议：在“内存末日”式涨价周期中，这类单品促销和组合优惠是购买新内存的最佳途径。429美元对32GB仍显昂贵，但已是当前 Newegg/Amazon 上最低价的 DDR5-6000 CL30 选择，且无需在合理时序、速度和价格之间做太大妥协。若计划组建 DDR5 新平台或升级现有系统，尤其是 AM5 用户，可重点考虑。

history.title: MediaTek’s next-gen Dimensity CX C10 Max will power new Googlebook initiative alongside Intel and Qualcomm – 3nm SoC has similar specs to Kompanio Ultra in Chromebook Plus devices, despite claims of ‘elevating’ computing portfolio
history.description: MediaTek's next-gen Dimensity CX C10 Max will arrive inside Googlebook devices, featuring similar specs as the Kompanio Ultra 910 currently available.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Google’s “brand-new category of flagship laptops,” called Googlebooks, will contain MediaTek’s next-gen Dimensity CX C10 Max processor, the first SoC to launch in the Dimensity CX lineup. It’s built on a 3nm node (TSMC N3) and uses an all-performance-core design, packing eight cores on the CPU and 11 cores on the GPU, along with MediaTek’s NPU 890, delivering up to 55 TOPS of AI performance, according to MediaTek. The new CX lineup will sit between MediaTek’s other offerings, between the RTX Spark in higher-end laptops and Chromebook with Kompanio chips.MediaTek calls the C10 Max the “flagship of the lineup,” though we don’t have full specs on the chip, and not so much as a name for the other chips in the lineup. MediaTek is launching the CPU on the same day Googlebooks go on sale (September 21), and the company says it will power an upcoming Googlebook device. MediaTek hasn’t explicitly said that the chip is exclusive to Googlebook devices, though that seems likely given the company’s previous work with Google on Chromebooks.The C10 Max is an “all big core” CPU, according to MediaTek, but not all eight cores are equal. MediaTek is using three different core types: one Cortex-X925 core, three Cortex-X4 cores, and four Cortex-A720 cores. The Cortex-X925 is the successor to the Cortex-X4, with higher clock speeds, a larger 10-wide decode, and larger L2 cache. The Cortex-A720 fits in a different range, though it was succeeded in 2024 by the Cortex-A725. This core split is identical to what MediaTek has used in its Dimensity 9400, 9400+, and 9500s mobile chips (though, presumably, the C10 Max will be afforded a larger power budget and higher boost clocks).Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Perhaps more pressing, it’s identical to the core split in the Kompanio Ultra 910, MediaTek’s previous flagship in this category. The C10 Max features the same GPU and NPU, as well: the Arm Immortalis-G925 MC11 for the GPU and MediaTek NPU 890. The C10 Max also comes with the same 12MB of L3 and 10MB of system-level cache. The biggest difference, at least based on the specs MediaTek has shared, is memory speed. Both use LPDDR5X, but the C10 Max climbs up to 9,600MT/s from 8,533MT/s on the Kompanio Ultra 910. (Image credit: MediaTek)On performance, MediaTek has two rather vague claims, which you can see in the slide below. It claims the C10 Max has up to 15% faster multi-threaded performance and 50% lower power in single-threaded workloads, though without any mention of performance, compared to the Snapdragon X Elite X1E-84-100. That chip is the second from the top of Qualcomm’s last-gen X Elite stack, sporting 12 cores (8+4) and a 4.2 GHz boost clock. MediaTek says it used Geekbench 6.5 and ran the multi-threaded tests at iso-power, that being 12W (the X1E has a base TDP of 35W, and MediaTek didn’t clarify what power usage it was referencing). You may like Qualcomm details Snapdragon C specs for $300 laptops for the first time AMD's next-gen 10-core 'Medusa Point' APU shows up on Geekbench again, with its best score yet AMD's upcoming Zen 6 Medusa Point 10-core APU pops up on Geekbench Unfortunately, the performance numbers here aren’t worth much, at least not how they’re presented. Perhaps most notably, the test platforms were completely different, with MediaTek using a reference board running ChromeOS R133 for its chip and using a Galaxybook 4 Edge with Windows 11 from Samsung for Qualcomm’s chip. They’re only comparable on memory capacity (16GB) and battery (60Whr). MediaTek also didn’t share any actual numbers, leaving the claim about 50% lower single-threaded power usage dead in the water.During a press Q&A, MediaTek VP of computing platforms PD Rajput said the C10 Max is competing with the X1 Elite, not Qualcomm’s newer X2 series. “In the category of devices we’re looking at, and the segment we’re on, it’s the X1E we’re competing with.” MediaTek didn’t share any performance numbers comparing the C10 Max to x86 CPUs from AMD or Intel.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsRajput also said that the Dimensity CX C10 Max won’t flow down to Chromebook or Chromebook Plus devices, saying MediaTek is “elevating our compute portfolio” with the C10 Max. We asked if the chip will come to Windows laptops as well, and the company said it’s only confirmed for Googlebooks at this time. (Image credit: MediaTek)MediaTek says the C10 Max is capable of delivering up to 19 hours of battery life, which is certainly possible, though battery life is more of a system-level concern than a chip-level one. MediaTek arrived at that number testing a reference board with a 60Whr battery, so it's possibly the battery life could climb higher if the chip is paired with a larger battery.Full MediaTek Dimensity CX C10 Max presentation Image 1 of 16 (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) (Image credit: MediaTek) Image 1 of 16 View Original Image 2 of 16 View Original Image 3 of 16 View Original Image 4 of 16 View Original Image 5 of 16 View Original Image 6 of 16 View Original Image 7 of 16 View Original Image 8 of 16 View Original Image 9 of 16 View Original Image 10 of 16 View Original Image 11 of 16 View Original Image 12 of 16 View Original Image 13 of 16 View Original Image 14 of 16 View Original Image 15 of 16 View Original Image 16 of 16 View Original Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

history.titleZh: MediaTek’s next-gen Dimensity CX C10 Max will power new Googlebook initiative alongside Intel and Qualcomm – 3nm SoC has similar specs to Kompanio Ultra in Chromebook Plus devices, despite claims of ‘elevating’ computing portfolio
history.descriptionZh:
谷歌将其称为“全新品类旗舰笔记本”的 Googlebooks，将采用联发科下一代 Dimensity CX C10 Max 处理器。这是 Dimensity CX 系列首款 SoC，也标志着联发科进一步进军高性能 Arm 笔记本/ChromeOS 设备市场。新 CX 系列定位在联发科现有产品组合之间：高端笔记本中的 RTX Spark 与搭载 Kompanio 芯片的 Chromebook 之间。联发科称 C10 Max 是“该系列旗舰”，但未公布完整规格，也没有透露系列其他芯片的名称。联发科将在 Googlebooks 开售同日，即 9 月 21 日推出该 CPU，并表示它将驱动一款即将推出的 Googlebook 设备。联发科没有明确说该芯片仅限 Googlebook 设备，但鉴于其此前与谷歌在 Chromebook 上的长期合作，这种可能性很大。联发科计算平台副总裁 PD Rajput 还表示，C10 Max 不会下放到 Chromebook 或 Chromebook Plus，称联发科正通过该芯片“提升计算产品组合”；至于是否会用于 Windows 笔记本，目前仅确认 Googlebooks。

核心规格方面，C10 Max 基于台积电 N3 3nm 制程，采用“全大核”设计，CPU 为 8 核，GPU 为 11 核，并集成 MediaTek NPU 890，AI 算力最高 55 TOPS。不过，它的八颗 CPU 核心并非完全对等，而是分为三簇：1 个 Cortex-X925、3 个 Cortex-X4 和 4 个 Cortex-A720。Cortex-X925 是 Cortex-X4 的后继，具备更高时钟频率、更大的 10 宽解码和更大的 L2 缓存；Cortex-A720 则定位不同，且已在 2024 年被 Cortex-A725 取代。这一核心拆分与联发科 Dimensity 9400、9400+、9500s 移动芯片相同，推测 C10 Max 会获得更大功耗预算和更高加速频率。更关键的是，它与联发科上代同类旗舰 Kompanio Ultra 910 高度相似：相同 CPU 核心拆分、相同 Arm Immortalis-G925 MC11 GPU、相同 NPU 890，以及相同的 12MB L3 和 10MB 系统级缓存。最大区别在于内存速度：两者均使用 LPDDR5X，但 C10 Max 从 Kompanio Ultra 910 的 8,533MT/s 提升到 9,600MT/s。

性能对比上，联发科给出了两个较模糊的说法：与骁龙 X Elite X1E-84-100 相比，C10 Max 多线程性能最高快 15%，单线程负载功耗低 50%，但没有提供单线程性能数据。X1E-84-100 是高通上代 X Elite 中第二高型号，拥有 12 核（8+4）和 4.2GHz 加速频率，基础 TDP 为 35W。联发科称使用 Geekbench 6.5，并在 12W 等功耗下运行多线程测试，但未说明具体参考功耗。这些数据参考价值有限：测试平台完全不同，MediaTek 使用运行 ChromeOS R133 的参考板，高通使用三星 Galaxybook 4 Edge 运行 Windows 11；两者仅在 16GB 内存和 60Whr 电池上相同。联发科也未分享任何绝对数字，因此“单线程功耗低 50%”的说法难以验证。在发布会问答中，Rajput 表示 C10 Max 竞争的是 X1 Elite，而非高通更新的 X2 系列；“在我们关注的设备类别和细分市场中，我们竞争的是 X1E。”联发科也没有提供与 AMD 或 Intel x86 CPU 的性能对比。

技术影响和应用场景方面，C10 Max 的 55 TOPS NPU 面向本地 AI 工作负载，配合 Googlebooks 试图在 Arm 高性能笔记本和 ChromeOS 旗舰市场中挑战高通。联发科称该芯片可提供最高 19 小时续航，但这是基于 60Whr 电池参考板的系统级测试结果；续航还取决于整机设计，若搭配更大电池可能更长。总体来看，C10 Max 是联发科提升计算产品线定位、绑定谷歌 Googlebook 的关键产品，但其公开规格与上代 Kompanio Ultra 910 差异有限，主要升级集中在内存速度和产品定位；实际性能、功耗和 AI 体验仍需真机验证。

history.title: PlayStation 3 emulation devs work around an Nvidia bug for up to 37% faster performance — open-source coders reach out to Nvidia to over uncovered bug
history.description: The developers of RPCS3 have found a workaround for an Nvidia driver bug and are touting up to 37% performance gains.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The developers of the open-source PlayStation 3 emulator RPCS3 are celebrating finding a workaround for an Nvidia driver bug. The social media celebration stems from their testing showing that some PC configurations with Nvidia GPUs can enjoy up to 37% faster gaming performance. That’s more than a small wrinkle that’s been ironed out.Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs (Image credit: Noctua)Desktop GPU RoadmapNvidia's Enterprise GPU RoadmapTesting DirectStorage with GPU decompressionThe GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026?Rubin in-depthThe Stout Owl: The ultimate Noctua G2 PCMore RPCS3 performance on NVIDIA GPUs!Yahfz found a workaround for an @NVIDIA driver bug that was bottlenecking performance.In this boat test scenario:13900K + RTX 3080: +20% FPS9800X3D + RTX 5090: +25% FPSAMD GPU drivers do not have this bug, thus seeing no change. pic.twitter.com/BRad9AyesfSeptember 16, 2026We don’t know the exact nature of the Nvidia driver bug here, but the RPCS3 devs say that it bottlenecks the performance of their PS3 emulator. The first example cited provides two PC configurations running Red Dead Redemption in a scene featuring a paddle steamer. This is a popular ‘benchmarking’ scene focused on the Blackwater docks in the game, featuring relatively consistent camera paths and water effects. Swipe to scroll horizontally RDR boat test Configuration Performance uplift System 1 13900K + RTX 3080 20% FPS System 2 9800X3D + RTX 5090 25% FPS Those are very gratifying performance uplifts resulting from a driver bug workaround. Plenty of readers are probably more interested if the purported bug might also be bottlenecking native PC gaming performance. If it were, that would be a hugely significant find/workaround from the RPCS3 team, specifically ‘Yahfz.’ Please note that “AMD GPU drivers do not have this bug, thus seeing no change,” say the emulator developers.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Gran Turismo 5 ran 37% faster, used far less VRAMFollow-up social media postings underline that RDR isn’t an outlier, and “most games are impacted” by the bottleneck in the Nvidia driver. Great frame rate improvements can also be seen when using lower-end GPUs, too. The open sourcerers tested Gran Turismo 5 and saw frame rates climb by an incredible 37%, while VRAM usage dropped from 7.1 to 4.8GB. Meanwhile, playing Saints Row IV on a more mainstream GTX 1060 saw a 20% improvement in performance.Sadly, RPCS3 dev reach-outs to Nvidia are falling on deaf ears. Another follow-up tweet states that “We tried using the developer forums in the past to no avail and gave up.” It then asks @Nvidia to establish a direct communication channel to receive driver bug reports. Nvidia Software QA boss Manuel Guzman has now replied directly, so we will see what happens in due course. history.titleZh: PlayStation 3模拟器开发者绕过Nvidia漏洞，性能提升高达37%——开源编码人员就发现的漏洞联系Nvidia
history.descriptionZh:
开源 PlayStation 3 模拟器 RPCS3 的开发团队宣布，他们找到了一种绕过 Nvidia 显卡驱动 bug 的变通方案，使部分 Nvidia GPU 配置在运行 PS3 游戏时获得最高 37% 的帧率提升。该发现由开发者 Yahfz 完成。此前，Nvidia 驱动会在 RPCS3 中造成性能瓶颈，而 AMD GPU 驱动不存在这一问题，因此 AMD 平台没有出现类似变化。

测试使用《Red Dead Redemption》（《荒野大镖客：救赎》）中 Blackwater 码头附近的“船测试”场景，该场景相机路径和水面效果相对稳定，常被用于基准测试。结果显示，i9-13900K + RTX 3080 配置的 FPS 提升 20%，Ryzen 7 9800X3D + RTX 5090 配置的 FPS 提升 25%。开发团队并未披露 Nvidia 驱动 bug 的具体技术细节，但指出该瓶颈会拖累模拟器性能。其变通方案是在模拟器侧规避驱动中的低效路径，而不是等待 Nvidia 发布官方修复。由于 PS3 模拟器需要将 Cell 处理器和 RSX GPU 的指令、图形调用转换为 PC 的 x86 架构和现代图形 API，对驱动路径、同步和显存管理非常敏感，因此驱动层低效可能被明显放大。

后续测试表明，《Red Dead Redemption》并非孤例，“大多数游戏都受到影响”。在《Gran Turismo 5》中，帧率提升高达 37%，同时显存占用从 7.1GB 降至 4.8GB。在较主流的 GTX 1060 上运行《Saints Row IV》也有 20% 的性能提升。低端 GPU 同样能从这一变通方案中受益。

这一发现的影响不仅限于 RPCS3 玩家。开发团队提出，如果同一 Nvidia 驱动 bug 也会拖累原生 PC 游戏，那么其意义将远超模拟器领域。不过目前证据主要集中在 RPCS3 这类非原生工作负载上。沟通方面，RPCS3 开发者称过去通过 Nvidia 开发者论坛报告问题没有效果，已放弃该渠道，并公开呼吁 Nvidia 建立直接沟通渠道接收驱动 bug 报告。Nvidia 软件质量保证负责人 Manuel Guzman 已直接回复，后续进展有待观察。对于 PS3 模拟器用户和 Nvidia GPU 玩家而言，这一发现已经带来可观的性能与显存效率提升；若 Nvidia 进一步修复驱动，其影响可能扩展到更广泛的 PC 图形生态。

history.title: Hands-on with Googlebooks — Five models, the new Googlebook OS, and a Mac-style experience for Android users at premium prices
history.description: Google has detailed its new Googlebooks, five laptops combining Android and ChromeOS to make a Mac-like experience for Android users, with a ton of Gemini tacked on.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter After a brief tease back in May, Google is detailing its lineup of Googlebooks, its new line of laptops designed to serve as premium systems that work best with Android phones and deliver unique abilities through Gemini.At an event ahead of the launch, Sameer Samat, Google's president of the Android ecosystem, said that the device's new OS would pull from the best aspects of ChromeOS and Android to design a modern (Image credit: Google)The systems are available for pre-order today and will land in stores on October 4 in the U.S. and October 5 in Canada, the U.K., Ireland, France, Germany, and Australia.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Googlebook hardwareThe first five Googlebooks come from five partners: Dell, Lenovo, HP, Asus, and Acer, and offer silicon from either Intel or Qualcomm. MediaTek is also listed as a partner, but its chips aren't in the first wave of devices.These devices are clearly designed to go after the MacBook Air and premium Windows laptops, using materials like aluminum, magnesium, and carbon fiber rather than plastic. The screens are all high-resolution, with several 2880 x 1800 OLED screens. Most of the lineup has haptic touchpads. You may like Best of IFA 2026: MacBook Neo competitors, monitors, and wild laptop concepts MediaTek next-gen Dimensity CX C10 Max will power new Googlebook initiative HP OmniBook X Flip 14 Review: Premium design, middling performance Google has set a floor of 16GB for RAM, with several of the options offering up to 32GB. 256GB is the minimum for storage, though many go up to 512GB, and Dell and HP go up to 1TB. Swipe to scroll horizontally Row 0 - Cell 0 HP Googlebook 14 Dell XPS Googlebook Lenovo Googlebook 15 Acer Googlebook 14 Asus Googlebook 14 CPU Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite X1E-80-100 Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite Intel Core Ultra 5 and 7 (Panther Lake) Intel Core Ultra 5 processor 325 or Intel Core Ultra 7 processor 355 Intel Core Ultra 5 processor 325 or Intel Core Ultra 7 processor 355 RAM 16GB - 32GB 16GB - 32GB 16GB 16GB 16GB - 32GB Storage 256GB - 1TB 512GB - 1TB 256GB - 512GB 256GB - 512GB 256GB - 512GB Display 14-inch, 2880 x 1800, OLED, touch, 500 nits 13-inch, 2560 x 1600, touch, 500 nits 15.3-inch, 2880 x 1800, OLED, touch 14-inch, 2880 x 1800, touch, 500 nits 14-inch, 2880 x 1800, OLED, touch, 500 nits Biometric Login Fingerprint sensor, Fingerprint sensor, IR camera Fingerprint sensor, IR camera Fingerprint sensor Fingerprint sensor Weight 2.7 pounds / 1.22 kg 2.5 pounds / 1.13 kg 2.68 pounds / 1.22 kg 2.7 pounds, 1.22 kg 2.2 pounds / 1 kg Starting price $1,299 $1,199 $1,299 $899 $1,299 All of them also feature a Glowbar (a throwback to the Chromebook Pixel and Pixel C tablet), a series of RGB lights on the lid that glows playfully at startup, shows battery charge, and can react when you talk to Gemini. Given that the Glowobar is behind the screen, we'll see how much use it gets, but Google says it's going to open an API for developers.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsSeveral of the new laptops are reminiscent of existing Windows machines. The HP Googlebook 14 resembles the HP OmniBook Ultra, while the Dell's XPS Googlebook is effectively this year's XPS 13. The Asus Googlebook 14 is a dead ringer for the premium, enterprise-focused ExpertBook Ultra.And yet some of those familiar looks were my favorites on first impression. I particularly appreciated how thin and light both Asus and Dell's designs are, though Asus' has far more ports. With the exception of Acer's 2-in-1, the entire lineup consists of clamshell designs.The laptops aren't cheap, particularly if you're used to the lower end of Chromebooks. The cheapest notebook, the Acer Chromebook 14, starts at $899, though the notebook maker says it's a limited-time price. The XPS starts at $1,199, while the rest all start at $1,299, the price of a base MacBook Air. What to read next The bifurcated laptop landscape of Computex 2026 – MacBook Neo competitors with 8GB of RAM, and expensive Nvidia laptops promising an agentic-focused future of Windows on Arm HP OmniBook Ultra 14 review: Potent Snapdragon performance, great endurance, premium pricing At IFA 2026, computing chased the high and low ends — AI and budget-focused machines left little for the rest of us (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Google's keyboard layout brings back the caps lock key (which also doubles as the Quick Insert key, see below), and also adds a G key that brings up the launcher.Meet the Googlebooks*️⃣ Acer Googlebook 14 Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original *️⃣ Dell XPS Googlebook Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original *️⃣ Asus Googlebook 14 Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original *️⃣ Lenovo Googlebook 15 Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original *️⃣ HP Googlebook 14 Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Googlebook OSThe Googlebook OS is designed to be tightly integrated with your existing Android phone. The idea is that once you log in and set up the laptop for the first time, you'll find all of your files, photos, apps, emails, and saved passwords right where you would expect them, with changes flowing back to your phone. The whole idea seems very Mac-like, but for Android, which never had that same tight integration with Microsoft's Windows, despite multiple attempts.In general, this seems like a simple but mostly full-featured desktop OS for the crowd growing out of Chromebooks. Much of the work still occurs in your browser (in this case, Chrome), but there's a full file manager (including AI descriptions of files) to open files locally. You can put phone-style widgets on your desktop, and there's a taskbar at the bottom of the screen.(Image credit: Google)The applications, however, all come from the Android side of things. Google provides apps through the Play Store. Google is counting on a mix of the Play Store and web apps, meaning you won't be downloading any executables to use on a Googlebook from the web. Google claims that 70% of time on a laptop is spent in a web browser.The company is highlighting Adobe's Photoshop and Lightroom, CapCut, Netflix, and Disney+ (with offline viewing). Those apps, among others, will have a desktop mode. Additionally, Google says that half of the 100 top games on Android are "already optimized for keyboard, mouse, and large screen, with new games launching monthly."That latter point is quite PC gaming, though. For that, Google is offering a free year of Nvidia GeForce Now, and suggests more gaming will come to Googlebooks soon enough. (Gaming Chromebooks didn't quite take off, so we'll see what Google does differently here).(Image credit: Google)There are a handful of features to move back and forth between your laptop and your phone that seem helpful (and again, quite similar to macOS). Continue On is effectively macOS and iOS's Continuity, which lets you pick up on a task from your phone on your laptop, and vice versa. The application for the file you're working on shows up in a Googlebook's taskbar. For when you want to use your phone directly on the laptop, Cast My Apps lets you control it from the desktop (similar to macOS's iPhone Mirroring) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Google also includes Antigravity, its platform for developing agentic workflows and agents to build web apps or Android software on your device. At an event ahead of the show, Googlers were vibe coding software to put on their machines, from a teleprompter Android app to an arcade full of '80s arcade games. Google says Antigravity will also include a Linux terminal environment to run tools like Claude CLI or Antigravity CLI.Google promises 10 years of support for Googlebook OS on a Googlebook, though at a press event, there was a big asterisk next to that claim. The 10 years starts from the launch of the platform and chip inside the Googlebook, I was told, which means that Intel's Panther Lake chips will have nearly a year lopped off immediately (they launched in January this year), while Snapdragon X Elite, which first shipped in 2024, will already be 2 years behind.This isn't terribly different from how Google supports its Chromebooks now — by platform, not launch of the system, but that difference may not play the same in the big leagues. Google keeps a database where you can see when any given Chromebook model will stop receiving updates, and presumably it will do something similar with Googlebooks.Gemini IntelligenceThe features that make Googlebooks stand out are the ones where Google baked its Gemini AI directly into the operating system. That also means how much you like a Googlebook may be directly tied to how useful you find these features.(Image credit: Google)The one feature Google talks up the most is the Magic Pointer. You wiggle your cursor, and it becomes a Gemini-focused pointer. Click on anything to get contextual suggestions or type into the assistant to get answers about what you chose. For example, one demo showed someone using Magic Pointer on a PDF of a calendar and asking Gemini to add the dates to their calendar. In many cases, it felt like a shorter way to get to Gemini than copying and pasting screenshots, but I didn't get enough time to judge how useful it could be.The Caps Lock key doubles as a "Quick Insert tool" — effectively a souped-up copy and paste that includes your clipboard history, emojis, translation tools, proactive assistant capabilities, and opens Rambler, which allows for text-to-speech and cleans up where you might have stumbled and messed up.Rambler was introduced at I/O this year and debuted on the Pixel 11, but it was impressive on the Googlebook. I tend to type rather than speak on a computer, but this might convince some people otherwise. It even did well in a relatively loud demonstration environment.While there are a number of widget options in Googlebook OS, you can also create your own with natural language. I was able to make one that showed me the top movie of the day in a given year.(Image credit: Google)Perhaps the most natural are Magic Cues — recommendations to do something with the information you're seeing — peppered throughout the OS. If you see dates, you may be cued to make a calendar invite. If someone asks a question in a text message, the answer might pop up if it is in your email, texts, or somewhere else it was discussed before. This has also been on Pixel phones before, but seems to fit in just fine on a laptop.Beyond the Gemini features, every Googlebook is shipping with 12 months of Google AI Pro (usually $19.99 per month), offering 5TB of cloud storage and advanced tools like higher rate limits in Gemini, entry rate limits to agent models in Antigravity, credits for use in Google Flow, and higher access to AI in Google Search. There are also 3 months of YouTube Premium, CapCut, and Photoshop. Additionally, there's 1 year of Gemini Spark, a version of the AI that acts as an autonomous agent. That's a lot of freebies, and it will be interesting to see how many people feel the need to keep and renew them to make the most of their Googlebooks.Can Googlebook break through?Despite Android's popularity globally, Chromebooks have largely been seen as kid stuff — quite literally for education. Googlebooks are a play to be more serious computers, but also bring a premium price.The AI features are neat in some cases, and showboaty in others. I need to spend real time with a Googlebook to truly decide what's useful.What is undoubtedly the most important part here is that Android users will have a device that integrates with their phones as well as Macs do with iPhones. Whether that's enough to justify a new operating system that still has some limitations is an open question. Again, we have to try these.Google clearly has some OEMs excited, but as computers get more expensive thanks to a component shortage, we'll have to see how these prices land, and if the company finally has a mainstream competitor on its hands.
